name: InterStim pivotal trials
question: Does sacral nerve stimulation improve refractory urinary urge incontinence compared with delayed implantation and continued standard therapy?

arms.label: delayed implantation with standard medical therapy

design.population: 76 test-stimulation responders with refractory urinary urge incontinence were randomized after baseline evaluation.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, open-label superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Schmidt 1999, PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods

verdictNote: All three primary diary measures favored immediate implantation at six months.
takeaway: Immediate InterStim sacral nerve stimulation versus delayed implantation with standard medical therapy significantly reduced daily urge-incontinence episodes, episode severity, and pad or diaper use at six months in test-stimulation responders (all P < 0.0001).

reports.label: Urge-incontinence randomized report
reports.citation: Schmidt RA, Jonas U, Oleson KA, et al. "Sacral nerve stimulation for treatment of refractory urinary urge incontinence." *J Urol.* 1999;162(2):352-357. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)68558-8
reports.followUp: 6 months randomized; efficacy appeared sustained for 18 months
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Materials and Methods and Results

results.note: The abstract does not give arm-specific diary means or a prespecified alpha.
The abstract does not give arm-specific severity scores.

results.note: A further 10/34 (29%) had greater than 50% fewer episodes.
